Your mission: you have learned functions, lists, dictionaries, loops, files, tests and games with keys and timers. Now you put them together in a program that is completely yours. In week 12 your family will come to our Family Arcade to play your game or make art with your studio, and you will explain how it works. You can work alone or with a partner.

Step 1: Choose your option

Option A: Arcade game Option B: Art studio
What it is A turtle game with keys, a timer and a score. A program that makes designs (often random) and can save and load them.
You will love it if… you like playing and inventing games. you like patterns, colors and surprises.
Starter file starter/ game_template.py starter/ art_studio_template.py
The file saves… high scores designs (one setting per line)

Step 2: Know the must-haves

Whatever you choose, your finished program must have all six. Check them off as you go.

TipThe secret of easy tests

Put the rules of your program (scores, moving, touching, saving) in small functions that do not use turtle. They take values in and return an answer, so they are easy to test. Keep the drawing in other functions.

Step 3: Get an idea

Pick one from the menu, change it, or invent your own.

How your project is assessed

Your teacher uses the same four questions. Check where you think you are now, and again at the end.

Just starting Getting there Got it Expert
Creativity I changed a few things in the template. My project has my own theme and one new idea. My project has its own idea, rules and look. My idea has a surprising twist that makes people want another go.
Working code It runs, but crashes or the main part does not work yet. The main part works; some must-haves are missing. It works as my pitch said, with all six must-haves. It also handles tricky moments (walls, missing file, playing again).
Code quality and tests My code is one long block; no tests yet. I use some functions; 1–2 tests pass. Small functions with clear names and comments; 3 or more tests pass. Rules are separate from drawing; my tests include edge cases.
Explaining it I can show what it does. With help, I can explain what one function does. I can explain how one part works and one decision I made. I can explain my design, what I would change, and a bug my tests caught.

Support and extension

Start from the template and change it step by step. Aim first for M2 (the core loop) and two tests; your teacher can be your navigator. A small project that works and that you can explain is a great project. Put your rules in their own file (like starcatcher_logic.py in the reference game) and import it. Add levels, a start menu, a top-5 high-score table, or let players choose their own keys. Write a test for your file functions.

When you are stuck

  1. Read the error message: start with the last line.

  2. Print the values: print("x is", x).

  3. Explain your code line by line to your partner or a rubber duck.

  4. Make the problem smaller: test one function on its own.

  5. Check the cheat sheet and the starter/README.md.

  6. Ask your teacher: say what you expected and what happened instead.

SafetyShowcase safety

Use a nickname on screen and on your project card. Your project stays on our computers and is shown to family only: nothing is uploaded. Credit anyone whose ideas, art or code you used.

Final project starter: Arcade Game or Art Studio

You get to build your own program! Pick ONE option:

Option Start from What it does now
A. Arcade game game_template.py Arrow keys move a square; touch the coin before the 30-second timer runs out.
B. Art studio art_studio_template.py n draws a new random flower, s saves it to my_design.txt. Loading (l) is your TODO.

Getting started (5 minutes)

  1. In Finder, make a new folder for your project, for example my-project-ada (use your nickname, not your full name).
  2. Copy your template and my_tests.py into that folder.
  3. Rename the template to your game's name, for example space_snack.py. Use lowercase letters and underscores, no spaces.
  4. Open it in Thonny and press the green Run button. Click the turtle window once so it can hear your keys.
  5. Read the TODOs from top to bottom. Do them one at a time and press Run after every small change.

Your project must have

Running your tests

  1. Open my_tests.py. Change the import line to your program's file name (without .py).
  2. Press Run. Every test should say PASSED.
  3. If Thonny says No module named pytest: Tools > Manage packages..., type pytest, click Search, then Install. No account needed.

Tip: put the rules of your program (scores, moving, touching) in small functions that do not use turtle. Those are easy to test.

Stuck?

  • Nothing happens when you press a key: did you call screen.listen()? Did you write onkey(go_left, "Left") without () after go_left?
  • FileNotFoundError: the file does not exist yet. Catch it with try / except FileNotFoundError and start with an empty list.
  • The program freezes: a while loop never ends. Press the red Stop button and check that something inside the loop changes.
  • Ask your partner to be the "rubber duck": explain your code line by line.

art_studio_template.py

"""MY ART STUDIO - starter template (project option B).

Run it first! Click the window, then press:
    n   make a new random design
    s   save the design in my_design.txt (next to this program)
    l   load the saved design          (TODO 2 makes this work)
Then make it YOUR studio by working through the TODOs.

Project checklist - your finished studio needs all of these:
  [ ] functions with parameters that return values (random_design ...)
  [ ] a list        (PALETTE - TODO 3: a list of designs, a gallery)
  [ ] a dictionary  (each design is a dict)
  [ ] a while loop  (draw_spiral)
  [ ] a file        (save works; TODO 2: make load work)
  [ ] 3+ tests      (my_tests.py)
"""

import random
import turtle
from pathlib import Path

# Okabe-Ito colors: safe for color-blind viewers.
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

# The saved design sits in the same folder as this program.
SAVE_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "my_design.txt"

view = {}                 # the screen and the turtle
current = {}              # the design on the screen right now


# ---------- RULES: pure functions, no turtle. Test them in my_tests.py.

def random_design():
    """Return a new design: a dictionary of settings."""
    # TODO 1: add your own keys, e.g. "background" or "stroke".
    return {
        "petals": random.randint(3, 12),
        "size": random.randint(60, 180),
        "color": random.choice(PALETTE[:7]),
    }


def design_to_text(design):
    """Turn a design into text, one "key=value" line per setting."""
    lines = []
    for key, value in design.items():
        lines.append(f"{key}={value}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def text_to_design(text):
    """The opposite of design_to_text: turn the text back into a dict."""
    design = {}
    # TODO 2: for each line in text.split("\n"):
    #   skip empty lines; split the line at "=" into key and value;
    #   if value.isdigit(), turn it into an int; put it in design[key].
    return design


# ---------- DRAWING AND KEYS

def draw_spiral(t, size):
    """A small spiral in the middle. It grows WHILE it is smaller than size."""
    t.penup()
    t.goto(0, 0)
    t.pendown()
    length = 2
    while length < size / 4:
        t.forward(length)
        t.left(30)
        length = length + 1


def draw_design(t, design):
    """Draw one design: petals in a circle, then a spiral."""
    t.clear()
    t.color(design["color"])
    t.pensize(2)
    for _ in range(design["petals"]):
        t.penup()
        t.goto(0, 0)
        t.pendown()
        t.circle(design["size"] / 2, 120)   # one side of a petal
        t.left(60)
        t.circle(design["size"] / 2, 120)   # the other side
        t.left(60 + 360 / design["petals"])
    draw_spiral(t, design["size"])
    view["screen"].update()


def new_design():
    current.clear()
    current.update(random_design())
    draw_design(view["artist"], current)


def save_design():
    with open(SAVE_FILE, "w") as file:
        file.write(design_to_text(current))
    print("Saved to", SAVE_FILE.name)


def load_design():
    try:
        with open(SAVE_FILE) as file:
            design = text_to_design(file.read())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Nothing saved yet - press s first.")
        return
    if not design:
        print("TODO 2: finish text_to_design so loading works.")
        return
    current.clear()
    current.update(design)
    draw_design(view["artist"], current)


def start_studio():
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.setup(600, 600)
    screen.title("My Art Studio")
    screen.tracer(0)
    artist = turtle.Turtle()
    artist.hideturtle()
    view.update(screen=screen, artist=artist)
    screen.onkey(new_design, "n")
    screen.onkey(save_design, "s")
    screen.onkey(load_design, "l")
    # TODO 3: keep a LIST of designs (a gallery) and press g to show them.
    screen.listen()
    new_design()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_studio()
    turtle.done()

game_template.py

"""MY ARCADE GAME - starter template (project option A).

Run it first! Click the window, then use the arrow keys to move the square
and touch the coin before the time runs out. Then make it YOUR game by
working through the TODOs from top to bottom.

Project checklist - your finished game needs all of these:
  [ ] functions with parameters that return values (clamp, is_touching ...)
  [ ] a dictionary  (SETTINGS - add your own keys)
  [ ] a game loop   (game_loop + countdown use ontimer)
  [ ] a list        (TODO 3)
  [ ] a file        (TODO 4: save the high score)
  [ ] 3+ tests      (my_tests.py)
"""

import random
import turtle

# Okabe-Ito colors: safe for color-blind players. Use shapes too!
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

# TODO 1: change these numbers and see how the game feels.
SETTINGS = {
    "step": 20,          # pixels per key press
    "wall": 270,         # the player stays between -wall and +wall
    "reach": 25,         # this close counts as touching
    "time_limit": 30,    # seconds in one game
    "tick_ms": 50,       # milliseconds between game-loop ticks
}

game = {"score": 0, "time_left": SETTINGS["time_limit"], "running": True}
view = {}   # the screen and turtles, filled in by setup_window()


# ---------- RULES: pure functions, no turtle. Test them in my_tests.py.

def clamp(value, low, high):
    """Return value, but never less than low and never more than high."""
    if value < low:
        return low
    if value > high:
        return high
    return value


def is_touching(x1, y1, x2, y2, reach):
    """True when point (x1, y1) is within reach of point (x2, y2)."""
    distance = ((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2) ** 0.5
    return distance <= reach


def add_points(score, points):
    """Return the new score."""
    return score + points


# TODO 4: write load_high_score(filename) and save_high_score(filename, score).
# Hint: look back at your week 7 work. Open with "w" to write. Reading a file
# that does not exist yet gives FileNotFoundError - use try/except.


# ---------- DRAWING AND KEYS

def setup_window():
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.setup(600, 600)
    screen.title("My Arcade Game")
    screen.tracer(0)

    player = turtle.Turtle()
    player.shape("square")
    player.color(PALETTE[4])
    player.penup()

    coin = turtle.Turtle()
    coin.shape("circle")
    coin.color(PALETTE[0])
    coin.penup()

    hud = turtle.Turtle()
    hud.hideturtle()
    hud.penup()

    screen.onkey(go_left, "Left")
    screen.onkey(go_right, "Right")
    screen.onkey(go_up, "Up")
    screen.onkey(go_down, "Down")
    screen.listen()
    view.update(screen=screen, player=player, coin=coin, hud=hud)


def move(dx, dy):
    """Move the player, but keep it inside the walls."""
    player = view["player"]
    wall = SETTINGS["wall"]
    x = clamp(player.xcor() + dx, -wall, wall)
    y = clamp(player.ycor() + dy, -wall, wall)
    player.goto(x, y)


def go_left():
    move(-SETTINGS["step"], 0)


def go_right():
    move(SETTINGS["step"], 0)


def go_up():
    move(0, SETTINGS["step"])


def go_down():
    move(0, -SETTINGS["step"])


def place_coin():
    wall = SETTINGS["wall"]
    view["coin"].goto(random.randint(-wall, wall), random.randint(-wall, wall))


def draw_hud():
    hud = view["hud"]
    hud.clear()
    hud.goto(-280, 260)
    hud.write(f"Score: {game['score']}   Time: {game['time_left']}",
              font=("Arial", 16, "bold"))


def game_loop():
    """Runs every tick_ms milliseconds while the game is running."""
    if not game["running"]:
        return
    player, coin = view["player"], view["coin"]
    if is_touching(player.xcor(), player.ycor(), coin.xcor(), coin.ycor(),
                   SETTINGS["reach"]):
        game["score"] = add_points(game["score"], 1)
        place_coin()
    # TODO 3: make a LIST of enemies (or extra coins). Move each one here
    # with a for loop, and check if the player touches it.
    draw_hud()
    view["screen"].update()
    view["screen"].ontimer(game_loop, SETTINGS["tick_ms"])


def countdown():
    """Runs once a second: the clock goes down until it reaches 0."""
    game["time_left"] = game["time_left"] - 1
    if game["time_left"] <= 0:
        game["running"] = False
        draw_hud()
        view["hud"].goto(0, 0)
        view["hud"].write("TIME UP!", align="center", font=("Arial", 24, "bold"))
        # TODO 4: save the score here if it is a new high score.
        # TODO 5: press space to play again.
        view["screen"].update()
    else:
        view["screen"].ontimer(countdown, 1000)


def start_game():
    setup_window()
    place_coin()
    draw_hud()
    view["screen"].ontimer(game_loop, SETTINGS["tick_ms"])
    view["screen"].ontimer(countdown, 1000)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_game()
    turtle.done()

my_tests.py

"""MY TESTS - open this file in Thonny and press the green Run button (F5).

pytest runs every function whose name starts with test_ and tells you
which ones PASSED and which FAILED. A test is a small check:
    assert <something that should be True>, "message if it is not"

1. Change the import below to YOUR program's file name (without .py).
2. Keep the example tests that still fit, delete the others.
3. Write at least 3 tests of YOUR OWN functions (TODO at the bottom).
   Test a normal case AND an edge case (a wall, zero, an empty list...).
"""

import art_studio_template as art
import game_template as game


# ---- Examples for option A (arcade game)

def test_clamp_leaves_a_good_value_alone():
    assert game.clamp(50, -270, 270) == 50


def test_clamp_stops_at_the_wall():
    # Edge case: past the wall on both sides.
    assert game.clamp(500, -270, 270) == 270, "Should stop at the right wall."
    assert game.clamp(-500, -270, 270) == -270, "Should stop at the left wall."


def test_touching_only_when_close():
    assert game.is_touching(0, 0, 10, 10, 25), "These points are close."
    assert not game.is_touching(0, 0, 100, 0, 25), "These points are far apart."


# ---- Example for option B (art studio)

def test_design_to_text_makes_one_line_per_setting():
    text = art.design_to_text({"petals": 6, "color": "#009E73"})
    assert text == "petals=6\ncolor=#009E73\n"


# When you have finished TODO 2 in art_studio_template.py, remove the #
# signs below: this test checks that saving and loading give back the same
# design (a "round trip").
#
# def test_text_to_design_undoes_design_to_text():
#     design = {"petals": 6, "size": 120, "color": "#009E73"}
#     assert art.text_to_design(art.design_to_text(design)) == design


# ---- TODO: YOUR tests. Copy this pattern:
#
# def test_what_should_happen():
#     result = my_function(some, values)
#     assert result == what_i_expect, "a helpful message"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import pytest
    pytest.main(["-v", __file__])
